    Executive summary

    Mandate: Mix (any). EXPOSURE: not computed - this board froze before the open (as_of 2026-10-12T12:53:04+00:00), and my EXPOSURE lesson binds a board that sits after the open; no figure is printed in its place. Regime: risk-on - SPY 778.57 at the freeze, +1.16% over 5d with trend up, ^VIX 15.51 after a +4.51% day, the US 10-year at 5.24 and the Dollar index at 102.39; the cycle composite projects +2.38% over the next 10 trading days, and CPI plus the MarketWatch bank-earnings preview sit inside this expiry week. The dispatch flags GS and UNH reports this week; my prompt serves no date for either, and neither name ships. Overnight: Asia closed down (-1.28% avg over 3: KOSPI -3.65%, Shanghai Composite -0.43%, Hang Seng +0.25%, the Nikkei 225 stale at -0.02%), Europe is up in session (+0.71% avg over 3: FTSE 100 +0.80%, DAX +0.76%, Euro Stoxx 50 +0.57%), and US futures are flat (-0.07% avg over 2: S&P 500 +0.04%, Nasdaq 100 -0.18%). Asia closed down hard while the futures sit flat and Europe trades up, and the Nasdaq lags the S&P: the regions disagree, the shape that most often retraces. Expected shape: a morning move that retraces and then reclaims. Gap: the dispatch says the gap block prints 'OPEN NOT YET PRINTED'; my prompt's gap_read rows print an open (TSLA: 'open 382.38 vs prior close 375.0'), which the Glazier and the Skeptic read as the stale 2026-10-09 print. My prompt wins on the figure, and no line of mine authors anything from the gap (R73, R87). Conviction is thin: 6 of 10 share lines sit at the 50.0 one-median, only CBOE 58.0 and GOOGL 55.0 separate from the pack, and the option column runs from 57.5 down to 46.0. Both columns are ONE bet - a long-equity tape through 2026-10-15: 10 share longs plus 9 calls, 10 + 9 = 19 lines of 20 long the underlying, with the CVS put the lone short; that is correlation, not a spread of independent bets, and the best expression of it is the room's own top of each column. The pyramid leader is The Black Swan, and its grades carry no extra weight (R33); it diverges from the room on the banks (SHARE=30 on WFC and BAC against one-medians 50.0 and 49.5) and on the WMT contract (78 against the room's 57.5). HOUSE RULES (decided before the open, never mid-session): (1) Stakes - every share line flat at 1.0 (R81); every leg at the 1.0 option default, the desk writing the owner's half on the 4 R4-OVERFLOW legs, with no chair override (R129); no add to any line, and no fresh ticket on a contract an open claim holds. (2) Exits - each leg runs on its EXIT token: a close through the ratchet level lifts that leg's stop to it, a CLOSE through the kill level kills the leg at the next open while an intraday print does not, and whatever is still open is closed at the else close (2026-10-15 for the 2026-10-16 legs, 2026-10-22 for AMZN and TSLA); share lines die only on their invalidation close. (3) Windfall - a leg whose premium closes at 2 x its freeze premium banks half at the first mark the desk serves for that contract and trails the rest at its ratchet; the banked half is never re-staked this week. Desk, R92/R12 - the memo's listings against the persisted book: share: PASS; option: DIFF PRINTED (R92) - UBER memo 57.5 / shipped 55.0, AMZN memo 56.5 / shipped 54.6, TSLA memo 54.0 / shipped 53.8, V memo 54.0 / shipped 53.8, RDDT memo 53.5 / shipped 53.6, PLTR memo 53.0 / shipped 53.4, CCI memo 51.5 / shipped 52.9, CVS memo 51.5 / shipped 52.9, HOOD memo 48.5 / shipped 51.9, SMCI memo 46.0 / shipped 51.0

    Lesson. THE MEAN SEES EDGE; A RANK OR A HIT RATE SEES GEOMETRY. Expected P&L is edge times stake and does not care about the shape of the bet, so the only scorer that can find edge in a key of mine is the mean of what its top five paid over its bottom five; a rank correlation or a reach count rewards shape. A ticket that needs a small move touches its level often with no edge at all: on run 54 WMT (VIG 0.66/1.75 = 0.38) closed 113.08 over its REACH-LEVEL 112.09 on the first close, while CVS, the same in-the-money shape as a put (|VIG| 0.47), lost 43.35% - so my 2026-10-07 branch (VIG<1 against VIG>1 reach rates) and my 2026-10-08 branch (capped against uncapped reach) would pass on geometry alone. Before I call two texts in conflict I name what each one governs: a rule that decides how a figure is stamped (R105, R125(v)) is not a rule that decides whether the figure may be filed, and where the stamp nulls nothing on my sheet (R116(iv)) its whole cost is a label.     Lesson. I date every footprint against the freeze before I read it, with a token called FLOW-CLOCK. Options trade only between 09:30:00 and 16:00:00, and the scanner's read time is not served to me (R133(g) NOT WIRED), so the freeze my prompt serves is my only clock. When the board froze before 09:30:00, every volume, every notable and the one-day move beside them belong to an earlier session, and the 2 DTE floor in OWNER and BAND does not refuse a notable that expires on the board's own date or later: it was bought in an earlier session and expires at or after the close the court scores, so it is a dated opener into the judged session, read through BAND's distance and MOVED-STRIKE like any other print - never called 'same-session', and never a bare 'dte 0' without the words BOARD CLOCK beside it. Where my prompt serves no freeze time, the token prints NOT SERVED and the floor reads as before. The mechanism: the floor exists to refuse a buyer who opens and closes inside one session; a buyer who carries a board-date expiry across the freeze has bet on exactly the session that is scored. Tonight it would have released two of the five notables I refused as 'dte 0': GOOGL (355.0C, 10460 on 3825, BAND IN, MOVED-STRIKE CLEAR) and NVDA (232.5C, 57191 on 16800, BAND IN, MOVED-STRIKE CLEAR); AMZN, TSLA and MSFT stay TRIPPED. Why it proves nothing: two rows, on the first board frozen before the open, on the night that showed the error - the rule corrects what my grade says about who traded, not tonight's rho. It earns an out-of-sample test over thirty OWNER rows on boards frozen before the open, counted in COURTS SAT (R56), not a claim. CHECK: grep tomorrow's sheet for FLOW-CLOCK. The first row prints 'FLOW-CLOCK PRE-OPEN|OPEN|NOT SERVED' with the served freeze time it read, copied as a literal. On a PRE-OPEN board any row that refuses a notable on the 2 DTE floor, or prints 'same-session' or a bare 'dte 0', fails outright, one violation enough; and the count of rows the clock released prints, so a night it releases none shows as a zero.

    Lesson. Read the clock, then size the overnight print before the story. Before I grade, I note whether my board froze before 09:30:00 ET, from the freeze time my prompt serves; if none is served I print FREEZE TIME NOT SERVED and take the after-the-open branch. BEFORE THE OPEN: the freeze mark is still the prior close, so the overnight foreign tape has yet to land inside the scored window. A foreign index or currency print of 2.0% or more is then a dated item at HOPS=1 for every row whose note names a chain through that market or its region (LINK=<market>-chain), whether or not a cause is served. I move that group together 3 points in the print's direction; 'no served cause' is never my reason to abstain on it. AFTER THE OPEN: the opening print has already carried that tape, so the print alone moves nothing. In both branches, a statement with no act (someone says, attacks or calls for), or an act my own note calls structural, status quo or not a catalyst inside the window, moves nothing: it files REF=median at most. This supersedes nothing, and HOPS=none stays ABSTAIN. Why: run 54 froze at 08:53:04 with freeze marks equal to the 2026-10-09 closes on 20 of 20 lines. I set KOSPI -3.65% aside on NVDA for want of a cause, and the four rows whose notes named an Asian chain fell: SMCI -4.49% (contract -64.35%), CSCO -2.58%, DELL -1.59%, NVDA -1.29% [W=426.9min 08:53:04->16:00:00]. Meanwhile the only two rows I moved were both wrong-signed: one on a Vance statement (MSFT 42 bear, +1.14%) and one on an EU quota I called structural (TSLA 55, contract -22.26%). Built this way, the sheet reads share +0.775 [n=4] and option +0.866 [n=3], against my undefined [n=1] and [n=2]. That is SEAT-COMPUTED, in-sample, hindsight from one night, and not a return claim. Pre-committed falsifier: if the moved print group's mean return sits on the wrong side of its column mean at two of the next three courts where the before-the-open branch fires, the branch retires. CHECK: on a board frozen before the open, a reviewer lists every foreign print of 2.0% or more my notes cite and expects one moved LINK group per print. On any board, the reviewer expects no moved row whose only item is a statement or an act my note calls structural (scripts/fd_check.py clause (n), to be added).

    Lesson. A BASE RATE THE PREMIUM ALREADY PAYS FOR IS A PRICE, NOT A GRADE. On 2026-10-12 [W=426.9min 08:53:04->16:00:00], with both authoring fields barred by a pre-open freeze, I filed every G_OPTION as 100 x the random-walk touch null to the break-even (CVS 84 down to AMZN 62). It ordered the day's reach - the four day-one touches (WMT, CBOE, CCI, V) all sat at 69 or above - and nothing the contract is scored on: rho -0.030 [n=6], my top line CVS 84 at -43.35%, and I sat above the room's median on 10 of 10 legs (one-median option rho +0.471 with me, +0.522 without). A touch null rises with nearness and with sigma, and the premium charges for both; my FILL clause already says P_touch authors nothing, and I broke it on the one grade the book ships. IF a row's only figure is a random-walk probability from the served sigma - touch, close or finish, to a break-even or to a lip - THEN G_OPTION=ABSTAIN (R61's per-line null, never a typed 50, R40), and the probability prints only as a dated claim for the R28 ledger: 'CLAIM: <TOUCH|FINISH> <level> by <date> sess=<n>: z |<x>| -> <tenth> -> <p>; null 2 x <p> = <q>', the z always printed as its absolute value, with 'lower tail' beside a level under the mark. A G_OPTION moves off that zero only by 100 x (my conditioned probability - the null), with the conditioning named on the row: a TAXON class that has earned authority under my 2026-09-29 rule. CHECK next court: option rows carrying a numeric G_OPTION and no named conditioning, target 0; my side_of_the_median count over the shipped legs; the one-median option rho with and without me; every dated CLAIM on the ledger and scored at its date with a touch Brier. I say three things against it. One: on most mornings it leaves my option column all-ABSTAIN and NON-FILING - I lose a vote and a rank, which is what a seat with no edge on that column should lose. Two: the null did carry information about reach (AUC 0.842 on day-one touches; 4 touches against 5.82 expected), so on a column scored on the size of the move it would earn a place; on a long-premium column scored on the signed contract it cannot. Three: one night, six legs, -0.030 inside any band - I am deleting a figure on doctrine, not on a record, and only the CLAIM ledger will show whether my touch nulls priced the reach better than the premium did.

    Lesson. A SHOCK'S OWN BID IS NOT A STEP. My slope - the ex-expiring front-minus-back that sets every step on my 30-60 ladder - may lift a row only where the name's last public move cannot account for it: before the sheet ships each row prints PRIOR=|pct_change_1d|/sigma as stated arithmetic from its own served fields (the sixty-session sigma_daily_pct; a row serving no sigma prints PRIOR NOT SERVED and moves nothing), and a row at PRIOR >= 1.00 files its slope step one lower (30 stays 30), on SHARE= and G_OPTION alike, because a front bid struck on a one-sigma public shock is that shock's realized vol - on a board frozen before the open it is the shock's own closing chain - and my charter says stand down when something public explains the premium. On 2026-10-12 I wrote that a public +15.6% day 'explains completely' CCI's 7.1 inversion and that AMZN's 3.2 followed a public +3.29%, then filed both at my top step 60 on those same slopes; the step-down (CBOE, BAC, CSCO, WFC in shares; AMZN, CCI, CVS, V on the legs) reads share +0.370 against the filed -0.059 [n=10] and option +0.120 against the filed +0.265 [n=6] (SEAT-COMPUTED) - a split inside one SE, not a proof. CHECK, one count before the sheet ships: rows at PRIOR >= 1.00 filed at their unadjusted slope step = 0 (2026-10-12: 9 of the 19 rows that printed a slope). KILL, in courts sat (R56), on the share column and on legs whose underlying moved at least 0.5% (R83): the rule dies if the unadjusted slope order outscores the stepped-down order over twenty courts.

The z I file ranked the six admitted contracts +0.200 (the cheap reaches did worse, SEAT-COMPUTED) while the contract tracked its underlying at +0.886 (columns.option_column.contract_vs_underlying_rho): one afternoon's mark is the underlying's direction, which a to-expiry ruler does not see. Two statements on my rows were wrong as written. My TSLA comment overruled a dispatch that said 'OPEN NOT YET PRINTED' with my gap block's 'open 382.38 vs prior close 375.0', which was session 2026-10-09's opening print, is_todays_bar false (day_report[ticker=TSLA].session_open.basis): it moved nothing, but the dispatch was right and I was not. And my highest G_OPTION, WMT 60, sat on WMT 2026-10-16 $110C, a contract r66-run52-WMT already held - as did the CBOE $300C, CSCO $120C and DELL $600C I also graded (court_orders.R114.a_picker_join_before_the_prompts.run_54_did); all four were share rows, so nothing scored, but I priced four contracts nobody could ship and never noticed.

    Lesson. A headline that names the ticker is not a mechanism until it carries a date inside my horizon, and tonight a name stood in for a date. MSFT took my only share departure, 34 and bear, on 'Vance says Microsoft replaced laid-off workers with foreign hires', a remark with no action and no date in the session, and rose +1.14%, second-best of ten; my whole share rho, -0.406 [n=10] [W=426.9min 08:53:04->16:00:00], is that row (UNDEFINED without MSFT). On the same sheet I called the 'AI FOMO' survey sentiment on AMZN and PLTR because it named no ticker, and let WFC and BAC off my no-mechanism clause on 'a print inside the window whose date my prompt does not serve' when the slate served an earnings date on 0 of 40 rows. Those three rows made +0.447% direction-signed against -0.771% for the other seven (SEAT-COMPUTED, n=10, SE 0.378). So from tomorrow: IF my case for or against a row rests on a news item - a remark, a preview, a survey, a column, a 'political attack', a print I place 'inside the window' - THEN it moves the SHARE view and G_OPTION only if I quote on that row a YYYY-MM-DD from my prompt on or before the row's horizon (the session for a share row, the expiry for an option row). Without that date it moves ZERO points in either direction and stays in the prose and key_risks, and the row's number comes from the served levels and the reach as my other rules say - never from my own median, because R61 bars the drift to the middle and R40 records a constant column as DID NOT FILE. CHECK, by someone who does not trust me: over the shipped rows, the Spearman of my share views against a 1/0 flag for 'my comment gives a news item as a reason for or against the row and prints no date for it' must sit inside +/-0.40 (tonight -0.509); outside that band the rule scores FAILED. KILL: it opens at 0 for 0, drawn in-sample on one moved row and two excused ones on a pre-open Monday when QQQ lost -0.696% over W; it is counted in COURTS SAT under R56, and if in four of the next five courts sat the rows I would have moved on an undated item go the way the item points against the rest on mean direction-signed return, undated news is informative and I delete the rule rather than renaming it.
